title: Saturday
text:
I got up early and walked barefoot

Through the corridors: I went down to the gardens

And kissed the plants

I absorbed the clean vapors of the earth,

Lying in the grass;

I bathed in the fountain that green cannas

Surround. Later, wet with water

I combed my hair. I perfumed my hands

With fragrant juice of jasmines. Fastidious, fine

Herons

Stole golden crumbs from my skirt.

Then I put on a dress of clarion lighter

Than gauze itself.

With a light leap I carried to the vestibule

My straw chair.

Fixed on the gate my eyes remained,

Fixed on the gate.

The clock told me: ten in the morning.

Inside a sound of china and crystal:

Dining room in shadow; hands preparing

Tablecloths.

Outside, sun like I have never seen

On the white marble of the staircase.

Fixed on the gate my eyes continued,

Fixed. I was waiting for you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the leisurely domestic ritual narrowing into the fixed act of waiting.

title: The Lost Caress
text:
The caress without cause slips from my fingers,

slips from my fingers... In the wind, as it passes,

the caress that wanders without destiny or object,

the lost caress—who will gather it?


I could love tonight with infinite pity,

I could love the first one who happened to arrive.

No one arrives. The flowered paths are alone.

The lost caress will roll... will roll...


If in your eyes they kiss you tonight, traveler,

if a sweet sighing shivers the branches,

if a small hand presses your fingers

that takes you and leaves you, that wins you and goes away.


If you do not see that hand, nor that mouth that kisses,

if it is the air that weaves the illusion of kissing,

oh, traveler, whose eyes are like the sky,

melted into the wind, will you recognize me?
editorial_note: This version keeps the same translated caress while preserving the source's separate catalog identity.

title: In the Ear...
text:
If you want to kiss me... kiss

—I share your whims—.

But do not make my mouth captive...

kiss me softly on the eyes.


Do not tell me of the spells

of your kisses on the neck...

my curls are jealous,

caress my hair.


For your timely pampering,

if your eyes are words,

they will give me, one by one,

the thoughts you shape.


Put your hand between mine...

they will tremble like a canary

and we shall hear the symphonies

of some thousand-year-old love.


This is a dead night

beneath the astral roof.

The orchard is silent

as in a lethal dream.


It has a hue of alabaster

and a mystery of pagoda.

Look at the light of that star!

I have it all in my soul!


Silence... silence... hush!

Even the water barely runs,

beneath its green screen

the sand almost quiets...


Oh! what delicate perfume!

Do not kiss my red lips!

In the platinum night

kiss me softly on the eyes...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated request for eye-kisses and the hushed platinum atmosphere.

title: Pain
text:
I would like on this divine October afternoon

to stroll along the far shore of the sea;

for the golden sand, and the green waters,

and the pure skies to see me pass.


I would like to be tall, proud, perfect,

like a Roman woman, to accord

with the great waves, and the dead rocks

and the wide beaches that gird the sea.


With slow step, and cold eyes

and mute mouth, let myself be carried;

see how the blue waves break

against the granites and not blink;

see how birds of prey eat

the little fish and not wake;

think that the fragile boats could

sink in the waters and not sigh;

see that the most beautiful man advances,

throat to the air, and not desire to love...


Lose my gaze, distractedly,

lose it and never find it again:

and, erect figure, between sky and beach,

feel myself the perennial oblivion of the sea.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the wish for cold, statuesque detachment beside the sea.

title: Journey
text:
Today the moon looks at me

white and measureless.


It is the same as last night,

the same as tomorrow.


But it is other, for never

was it so large and so pale.


I tremble as the lights

tremble over the waters.


I tremble as in the eyes

tears usually tremble.


I tremble as in the flesh

the soul knows how to tremble.


Oh! the moon has moved

its two silver lips.


Oh! the moon has told me

the three old words:


"Death, love and mystery..."

Oh, my flesh is ending!


Over dead flesh

my soul arches.


Soul — nocturnal cat —

leaps over the moon.


It goes through long skies

sad and curled up.


It goes through long skies

over the white moon.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the nursery-like repetitions turning into lunar disembodiment.

title: A Sun
text:
My heart is like a god without tongue,

mute it waits for the miracle,

I have loved much, every love was meager,

for every love I knew with want.


I have loved unto weeping, unto dying.

I loved unto hating, I loved unto madness,

but I await some nature-love

capable of renewing and redeeming me.


Love that fructifies my desert

and makes sensitive branches sprout from me,

I am a forest of living roots,

only the foliage tends to be dead.


Where is the one who encourages my desire?

Did the branches impoverish me in his eyes?

Vulgar obstacle, pale foliage

distinct from the faithful trunk that feeds it.


Where is the somber spirit

from whose opacity the flame may spring?

Ah, if he inflames my worlds with his love

I will be uncontainable as a river.


Where is the one who with his love will wrap me?

He must bring his great known truth...

Ice and more ice I gathered in life:

I need a sun to dissolve me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the heart as living roots waiting for a dissolving sun.

title: Ay!
text:
I shall be in your hands a fine cup

ready to sound when you wish to make it vibrate...

Springs will distill in it,

it will reflect the light that illumines you.


I shall be in your hands a fine cup.

You will have in it a gentle drink,

never sweeter, for pity grants it;

liquor that does no harm and forgives harm,

sweet liquor that knows of things...


You will have in it a gentle drink.

One dark day, between your long fingers

its gleaming crystal will be pressed

and the fine cup that gave you lethargies

will fall kindly into pieces;

one dark day, between your long fingers!


Formless crystal on the hard floor

shall not be cloudy because it is broken:

it will reflect the beatitude of heaven;

poor crystal thrown at your feet;

formless crystal on the hard floor.

May God forgive you damage so great:

blessed hands those that break it so,

may roses and lilies never thread them,

may eternal sweetness pay for its impiety.

May God forgive you damage so great...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the cup image through service, fracture, and forgiveness.

title: Your Plant
text:
Useless flight: the moon has already lost your spirit

and your song already has

silence for its wake.

Soon, rained star, vessel of nothing,


you will cloud some flowers or the gleam of a stone.


Not a murmur, not a tear multiplies your death,

not a sigh

sadly gives echo to your beak:

no one feels that you lose your place in the

air

and that, just as fish sleep among the waves

and men

within the earth, you have no rest

in the blue winds that

caress your wings.


And the clouds already know it is your last,

and that soon your mouth the

song of your life

will sing silently: but they keep their weeping,


but they keep their weeping for the olive groves.
editorial_note: The catalog title differs from the elegy-like bird text, so the translated body follows the source text.

title: House of Skin
text:
Wounded Bird


Useless flight: the moon has already lost your spirit

and your song already has

silence for its wake.

Soon, rained star, vessel of nothing,


you will cloud some flowers or the gleam of a stone.


Not a murmur, not a tear multiplies your death,

not a sigh

sadly gives echo to your beak:

no one feels that you lose your place in the

air

and that, just as fish sleep among the waves

and men

within the earth, you have no rest

in the blue winds that

caress your wings.


And the clouds already know it is your last,

and that soon your mouth the

song of your life

will sing silently: but they keep their weeping,


but they keep their weeping for the olive groves.
editorial_note: The embedded Wounded Bird heading is preserved because it appears in the source body.

title: Notes of a Life, Signs
text:
Notes of one life, signs

of another, if someone should read me

in this clumsy mirror

they will see their own face.




1974
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's short mirror-like turn intact.
